title: Kenyan Easter Coconut Fish
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Easter Coconut Fish — the traditional Easter Friday and Saturday fish dish. Rich, fragrant, and celebratory — fresh fish in a coconut milk and spice sauce, prepared with extra care for one of Kenya's most important religious holidays.
longDesc: Easter is one of the most significant occasions in Kenya's predominantly Christian calendar. The tradition of eating fish on Good Friday is widely observed, and Kenyan families prepare fish with particular care and ceremony during Easter weekend. The coconut fish preparation — rich, fragrant, and celebratory — is a favourite choice, bridging religious observance with culinary celebration.
ingredients: 1 kg firm fish fillets — snapper, kingfish, or tilapia
½ cup fresh coconut — grated, for garnish
steps: Season fish with salt, turmeric, and paprika. Set aside 15 minutes.
Heat oil. Cook onions until deeply golden — 8 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and chillies. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, curry powder. Cook 8 minutes until very thick.
Pour in coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add fish carefully. Spoon sauce over each piece.
Cover and simmer 10—14 minutes until fish is cooked through.
Add lemon juice. Garnish with coriander and fresh coconut.
chefTips: For Easter, use the finest, freshest fish available — the quality of the fish is the statement.
Fresh grated coconut as a garnish adds texture and fragrance that dried coconut cannot.
commonMistakes: Moving fish too early — it breaks apart.
cookingScience: Fish proteins denature at 60—65°C. The coconut milk sauce maintains a gentle simmering temperature well below vigorous boiling, keeping the fish proteins from over-tightening and producing perfectly moist, flaky fish.
sustainabilityTips: Choose sustainably caught fish for the Easter celebration.
culturalNote: Easter fish dishes represent the intersection of Christian tradition and Kenyan culinary culture — fish is the natural Easter food for a country with access to Lake Victoria, the Indian Ocean, and numerous rivers and lakes. Kenyan Easter fish is both religious observance and culinary celebration.
